title: Diagnose why clicking a Storybook story's button does not produce any entry in the Actions panel
objective: Owner reports (after the dev-server restart in the prior task): 'o action do botao nao funciona, talvez tenha um bug nele no geral' -- clicking the Button story still shows nothing in Storybook's Actions panel. Prior investigation (this session) confirmed via curl that storybook/test's fn() resolves correctly through Storybook's own __STORYBOOK_MODULE_TEST__ virtual module at the JS-module level, and that official Storybook docs say fn()-in-args should log to Actions with zero extra config -- but that was only a module-resolution-level check, not a real render-time/browser-level confirmation. This task investigates further: check the Storybook dev server's own log for addon/config warnings, inspect the actual preview bundle and any console-visible errors, and determine whether the args-to-props binding, the instrumenter, or some project-specific override (vite alias to dist/ instead of source, custom viteFinal, etc.) is preventing the click from ever reaching the fn() spy at all.
validations: DONE: read the running Storybook dev server's own log (previously silent, never checked this session) and found two real findings instead of guessing further from the browser side. Finding 1 (fixed): a genuine crash -- `TypeError: props.selection.selectedKeys is not iterable` inside DataTable, caused by the prior task's 'object' control fallback: Storybook's own Object control initializes its editable state to `{}` when an optional prop has no seed value in `args`, and that synthesized `{}` becomes a real prop value the component was never designed to receive (DataTableView unconditionally does `[...props.selection.selectedKeys]` once `props.selection` is not undefined). Fixed by only granting the 'object' control kind when the prop also has a real @example seed value; props with neither an example nor a safe representable value (DataTableProps.selection/pagination, EntitySummaryProps.tags) fall back to the pre-existing 'disabled' kind instead. Regenerated the mesh and verified directly: selection/pagination/tags now report 'disabled', rows/columns/panels (all of which have real @example values) keep 'object'.

DONE: rebuilt/typechecked architecture-studio clean after the fix; killed and fully restarted the Storybook dev server (not just HMR) with a clean log; confirmed via the fresh log that the crash no longer occurs and, with zero browser connections yet, there are zero occurrences of the second finding below (ruling out a server-startup-time cause for it).

FINDING (not fixed in this task, flagged for the owner to test): the earlier log capture (from the previous task's restart, before any code fix here) also showed a recurring `SecurityError: Blocked a frame with origin "http://localhost:6006" from accessing a cross-origin frame` inside Storybook's own internal Channel.emit -> PostMessageTransport.send -> stringify path -- the exact mechanism Storybook uses to send an 'action fired' event from the preview iframe to the manager UI's Actions panel. This only appeared after a real browser connected (zero occurrences from server startup alone in the fresh log), and is a strong candidate explanation for actions never appearing: apps/architecture-studio's /storybook route iframes Storybook from a different origin (127.0.0.1:4511 embedding http://localhost:6006 -- different ports are always cross-origin, regardless of hostname). If Storybook's manager attempts any window.parent/window.top-based communication assuming a same-origin embedding context, that access would throw exactly this SecurityError. Asked the owner to test by opening http://localhost:6006 directly in a new tab (bypassing the /storybook iframe) to confirm or rule this out -- not yet independently confirmed, since it requires a real browser session this agent cannot drive.
artifacts: packages/ui/scripts/export-doc-mesh.mjs (object-control fallback now requires a real @example seed value)
apps/architecture-studio/stories/data-table.stories.tsx + entity-summary.stories.tsx (regenerated with the corrected control kinds)
risks: The cross-origin SecurityError finding is diagnosed from a real server log capture, not fabricated, but its root cause (iframe embedding vs. some other trigger) is not yet independently confirmed via a controlled reproduction -- flagged clearly as unconfirmed rather than presented as fixed.

If the iframe-embedding theory is confirmed, the fix is likely outside this repo's control (a Storybook limitation/behavior when embedded cross-origin) rather than something adjustable via our own main.ts/preview.ts config -- would need further investigation of Storybook's embedding-detection code or an upstream issue search before attempting a fix.
